source.author: Al Brooks
source.chapter_title: Breakout Entries in Existing Strong Trends

conventions: stop entries mechanized as signal-bar-close then next-bar-open; every tunable constant is a parameter; long side only in pseudocode

candidates.name: TrendStrengthGaugeAtNewExtreme
candidates.quote: If the market moves far enough up for the breakout buyers to make at least a scalper's profit, then the breakout found more buyers than sellers ... if the market raced to a new swing high but then reversed down within a bar or two, then the breakout found more sellers than buyers.
candidates.description: Ongoing trend-strength gauge, re-evaluated at each new extreme: the trend is still strong only if recent breakouts beyond a prior extreme travel far enough, soon enough, for a scalper's profit; if a new extreme reverses quickly instead, treat the trend as weakening toward a trading range.
candidates.pseudocode: swingHigh = highest(high, swingLookback)[1]; highest(high, confirmBars) - swingHigh >= scalpTicks * tickSize
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (regime-strength filter re-applied at each new extreme)

complexity.reason: the same scalp-distance test as R02-06/R02-28, but applied repeatedly as a rolling trend-strength gauge rather than a one-time breakout check

candidates.name: TrendBarResetsPushCount
candidates.quote: smart money would not have bought the bar 11 breakout because it was a possible third push up after the exceptionally strong bar 6 breakout bar reset the count and formed the first push up.
candidates.description: An exceptionally strong, large-range trend bar resets the push/leg counter used to judge how extended a channel is — it becomes push #1 again rather than a continuation of the prior count.
candidates.pseudocode: close[0] > open[0] && (close[0] - open[0]) >= bodyFraction * (high[0] - low[0]) && (high[0] - low[0]) >= resetRangeMultiple * atr(atrLookback)
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (state-reset rule feeding a push/leg counter)

complexity.reason: an ATR-relative bar-size test that mutates persistent push-count state used by R02-37/R03-05

notes: Complements R03-15 (OutsideBarResetsLegCounter): here the reset trigger is an exceptionally large trend bar rather than an outside bar.

candidates.name: AvoidBreakoutBuyAfterTrendLineBreakRetest
candidates.quote: they would not have bought the bar 16 breakout, which was a higher high test of the old bar 14 high after a trend line break, since there was too much risk of a trend reversal.
candidates.description: Filter: block a with-trend breakout buy when it is really just a higher-high retest of a recent extreme that occurs after the trend line has already been broken — treat it as reversal risk, not fresh strength.

complexity.reason: needs trend-line projection from pivots plus a remembered prior swing high

candidates.name: ShortAtPriorHighWhenBreakoutWeak
candidates.quote: When traders think that a breakout looks too weak to buy, they will often instead short at and above the prior high.
candidates.description: When the bar breaking above a prior swing high is itself a weak breakout bar (small body, large tail), fade it by shorting at or slightly above that prior high instead of buying the breakout.
candidates.book_order_type: sell limit at or slightly above the prior swing high

complexity.reason: depends on the weak-breakout-bar primitive from chapter 2

candidates.name: ScaleInFadeAtSuccessiveSwingHighs
candidates.quote: Bears can make money on breakouts above prior swing highs by shorting the breakout and adding on higher. Then, when the market comes back to test the breakout, they can exit their entire short position and make a profit on their second entry.
candidates.description: Fade successive with-trend breakouts above prior swing highs by adding to a short at each new swing high, rather than taking one entry.
candidates.book_order_type: sell limit orders at or slightly above each successive swing high, adding to the position

complexity.reason: a scale-in entry evaluated at each of several remembered swing highs

notes: Countertrend mirror of R01-04's with-trend pyramiding; flag for the authoring pass the same way.

candidates.name: ExitFadePositionOnBreakoutRetest
candidates.quote: They would then try to exit all their short trades on a limit order at the original entry price, at the bar 7 high.
candidates.description: Exit the entire scaled-in fade position (R04-05) with a single limit order back at the first entry's price, once the market pulls back to retest the original breakout level.
candidates.book_order_type: limit order to cover at the first entry's price

complexity.reason: needs the first (not most recent) entry price remembered across a scale-in position

candidates.name: NextDayFollowThroughAfterTrendDay
candidates.quote: yesterday ... was a strong trend from the open bull trend day, so the odds were high that there would be enough follow-through today to close above the open, and even if there was a pullback on the open today, the bull trend would likely reach at least a nominal new high.
candidates.description: Filter/context: after a strong trend-from-open day, bias today with-trend, expecting today's close to finish above today's open, or at least a marginal new high, even through an opening pullback.

complexity.reason: depends on the 'trend day' design decision already flagged in R08-24

candidates.name: PauseBar
candidates.quote: Bar 4 was a pause bar just below yesterday's high, and buying one tick above its high is another good entry. A pause bar is a possible reversal setup
candidates.description: Shared primitive: a bar with a noticeably smaller range than the recent average — a brief stall that Brooks treats as a possible reversal/continuation setup.

candidates.name: BuyAbovePauseBarNearPriorHigh
candidates.quote: Bar 4 was a pause bar just below yesterday's high, and buying one tick above its high is another good entry ... going long where the early bears are buying back their shorts and where the longs who exited early would also be buying back their longs.
candidates.description: Buy above a pause bar that forms just below a significant prior high (e.g. yesterday's high), anticipating short covering and re-entry by longs who exited too early.
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the pause bar's high

complexity.reason: needs the pause-bar primitive plus a remembered significant prior high

candidates.name: NoCloseBelowEmaForNBars
candidates.quote: there had not yet been a close below the moving average and the market had been above the moving average for more than 20 bars, both of which are signs of strength.
candidates.description: Sign of strength: no bar has closed below the EMA for at least N bars — evidence the trend remains strong.

complexity.reason: an EMA plus a fixed-length existence scan for any violation

candidates.name: FirstCloseBelowEmaTwoBarReversalInsideBar
candidates.quote: Bar 9 was a bull inside bar after the first close below the moving average and the second bar of a two-bar reversal, so a breakout above the setup was expected to test the bull high at a minimum.
candidates.description: In a bull trend that has just posted its first close below the EMA in a long time, a two-bar reversal (down then up) whose second bar is a bull inside bar is a buy setup targeting at least the trend high.
candidates.pseudocode: close[2] >= ema(emaLength)[2] && close[1] < ema(emaLength)[1] && close[1] < open[1] && high[0] < high[1] && low[0] > low[1]
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above the inside bar's high

complexity.reason: combines an EMA-crossing state test with a two-bar reversal and an inside-bar pattern

rejected.quote: It is important to recognize that when a trend is strong, you can enter at any time and make a profit if you use an adequate stop.
rejected.reason: pure discretion with no bar-level test or threshold given for 'strong' or 'adequate'

rejected.quote: If you cannot process the two changes of direction reliably, do not take the countertrend trade; simply hold long.
rejected.reason: pure discretion about trader psychology/skill, not a bar-level test

chapter_summary: A short chapter on trading breakouts once a trend is already established. Beyond restating pullback-vs-breakout entry tradeoffs and the resting worst-case buy stop (already mined in R01-05), it contributes a rolling trend-strength gauge re-applied at each new extreme, a large-trend-bar push-count reset (complementing R03-15's outside-bar reset), a filter blocking breakout buys that are really post-trend-line-break retests, a scale-in countertrend fade with a single-price group exit, a pause-bar primitive with a near-prior-high buy setup, a 'no close below the EMA for N bars' strength sign, and a first-close-below-EMA two-bar-reversal inside-bar setup. Two purely discretionary/psychological statements were rejected.
